meta.title: Cross-check tolerances: invoice ↔ packing list ↔ CMR ↔ BYD (IM40)
meta.headline: NO official numeric tolerance found in Uzbek law for weight, value, quantity or package differences. Everything under 'proposal' is a YuklaGo product default, NOT law, and must be labelled so in the UI.

severity_levels.warning_ack: user must read and acknowledge (review screen Y13)
severity_levels.error_blocking: cannot proceed to signing until fixed or overridden with written reason

official_rules.finding: No official percentage or kg tolerance was found for differences in gross/net weight, quantity, number of packages or value between invoice, packing list, CMR and the BYD in: Customs Code, Instruction No. 2773, VMQ No. 605 (incl. Annex 1a). Searched 2026-11-18 (full-text keyword search + web search). Treat any difference as a discrepancy that must be explained or corrected.
official_rules.status: NOT FOUND – do not present any tolerance as law

official_rules.finding: Gross (grafa 35) and net (grafa 38) weights are rounded mathematically to 3 decimals (6 decimals if < 1 g).
Invoice value (grafa 42) and customs value (grafa 45) are rounded mathematically to 2 decimals; statistical value (grafa 46) to 3 decimals in thousand USD.
Quantity in supplementary unit: 2 decimals; below 0.01 → 6 decimals.
Grafa 22 total invoice value = Σ grafa 42; grafa 12 total customs value = Σ grafa 45; grafa 5 = number of grafa 31 items.

Gross = goods + all packaging needed to keep them intact until entering circulation, EXCLUDING containers and other transport equipment. CMR gross may legitimately differ if it includes pallets/transport equipment – reason must be shown.
Net = without any packaging, except inseparable primary retail packaging.

Road carrier must present CMR + commercial documents containing, among others: consignor/consignee, HS code (≥6 digits), gross weight (kg) and invoice value per code, number of packages, container numbers.

Invoice must contain 12 items: seller (name, address, TIN), buyer (name, address, TIN, phone), HS code ≥6 digits, origin country, description, invoice value, gross kg, net kg, total packages, quantity in supplementary unit, Incoterms (2010), contract number and date.
official_rules.ref: VMQ 605 Annex 1a (added by VMQ 630, in force 07.01.2025)

official_rules.finding: If the e-system finds errors, deficiencies or inconsistencies in the TED it is automatically returned with an e-notification stating reasons.
Automatic (no-officer) clearance requires, among others, no inconsistencies in TED data and consistency with permit documents.
Declarant may request amendment/addition of the TED if differences in quantity, name, description or other features are found during or after unloading into temporary storage.

Declarant may, with customs permission, voluntarily correct errors that do not affect payment calculation or prohibitions/restrictions before customs finds them; customs may allow fixing spelling errors in words (not numbers/letter codes) within one working day.

Customs adjusts customs value/payments if, among others, declared value does not match actual value because quantity and/or quality deviate from the contract (evidence: inspection act; agreed claim; expert opinion).
Incorrect declaration affecting payments/measures: MJtK Art. 227²² (confiscation + fine); not affecting the customs decision: 3 BHM (part 2) – per dars-01.

checks.rationale: Integer count; any difference means a lost/extra package or a document error. Art. 18 lists package count as mandatory carrier data.

checks.field: Gross weight – documents vs each other

proposal.label: PROPOSAL (product default, not law)
proposal.rule: diff = 0 → pass; 0 < diff ≤ 1 kg → info; diff ≤ max(1% of declared gross, 20 kg) → warning_ack (user must explain, e.g. pallets); otherwise error_blocking

formula.units: kg; every weight rounded to 3 decimals first (Instruction 2773 sub-point 30)
formula.declared: D = declared gross weight = invoice total gross (the figure that goes to Σ grafa 35); when evaluating per item use the item's invoice line gross
formula.pair: A, B = the two figures being compared, any pair from {invoice, packing list, CMR, Σ grafa 35}
formula.diff: diff = abs(A − B); T is ALWAYS computed from D (the invoice/declared figure), never from A or B
formula.decision: if diff == 0: pass; elif diff <= 1: info; elif diff <= T: warning_ack; else: error_blocking
formula.comparison_operators: '<=' is inclusive: diff exactly equal to T is a warning, not a block
formula.scope: evaluate every pair (invoice↔packing list, invoice↔CMR, packing list↔CMR, invoice↔Σ grafa 35) at shipment total and, where a document has lines, per item line; the worst severity wins
worked_examples: D=3798; A=CMR 3798, B=packing list 3780 → diff=18, T=max(37.98,20)=37.98 → warning_ack (Set C)
D=1344; A=packing list 1344, B=CMR 1430 → diff=86, T=max(13.44,20)=20 → error_blocking (Set B)

gross_weight_scope.official: Gross weight (grafa 35) = goods incl. all packaging needed to keep them intact until entering circulation, EXCLUDING containers and other transport equipment.
gross_weight_scope.ref: Instruction 2773, ch.5 p.25 sub-point 30 (grafa 35); same wording for export: ch.4 p.22 sub-point 30
gross_weight_scope.pallets: ⚠️ UNCONFIRMED: the Instruction does not name pallets. Whether a pallet is 'packaging' (included) or 'transport equipment' (excluded) is not settled in the text read; the UI must ask the user to state it and must not auto-subtract pallets.

checks.rationale: Grafa 35 excludes containers and other transport equipment, so CMR gross may differ by e.g. pallet weight (status of pallets unconfirmed). Large unexplained gaps trigger weighing/inspection risk. Thresholds are a product choice to separate rounding/pallets from real gaps.

checks.field: Net weight – invoice vs packing list vs GTD

proposal.label: PROPOSAL (product default, not law)
proposal.rule: diff = 0 → pass; diff ≤ max(0.5% of declared net, 5 kg) → warning_ack; otherwise error_blocking (no info tier for net)

formula.units: kg; every weight rounded to 3 decimals first (Instruction 2773 sub-point 33)
formula.declared: D = declared net weight = invoice net for that item line (the figure that goes to grafa 38); for the shipment total use invoice total net
formula.pair: A, B = the two figures being compared, any pair from {invoice, packing list, grafa 38}
formula.diff: diff = abs(A − B); T is ALWAYS computed from D (the invoice/declared figure)
formula.decision: if diff == 0: pass; elif diff <= T: warning_ack; else: error_blocking
formula.scope: evaluate per item line AND at shipment total; the worst severity wins (a per-line error is not hidden by a large shipment total)
worked_examples: Set C LED line: D=84; A=84, B=70 (packing list) → diff=14, T=max(0.42,5)=5 → error_blocking
Set C total: D=3234; A=3234, B=3220 → diff=14, T=max(16.17,5)=16.17 → warning_ack; worst = error_blocking

checks.rationale: Net weight is the base for kg-specific duty minimums (e.g. furniture 0.4 USD/kg) – tighter than gross.
checks.msg_uz: Netto vazn hujjatlarda farq qiladi: {a} va {b} kg.

checks.msg_ru: Вес нетто не может превышать брутто.
